package_contract.required: 403 safe denial; no unauthorized account/session creation or business writes.
package_contract.disposition: Retain failed status. SDK defaults or a narrower interpretation do not authorize weakening this accepted test.

baseline.conclusion: Source indicates pre-existing cookie-free protocol behavior, not a regression introduced by the R06 current-session repair. No before-repair runtime reproduction performed, so historical runtime equivalence is not certified.

protocol_facts.fact: Global origin validation skips safe methods; for mutating requests it normally checks Origin/Referer only when Cookie is present or forceValidate is true. The first-login form middleware checks cookie-bearing requests, blocks cross-site navigate Fetch Metadata and otherwise forces origin validation whenever any Sec-Fetch-Site/Mode/Dest is present; it returns without that validation when both cookies and fetch metadata are absent.

Credential sign-in accepts application/json and application/x-www-form-urlencoded, uses formCsrfMiddleware and native credential/account checks. It is public to the new application current-session gate.

BrowserContextAPIRequestContext uses APIRequestContext HTTP transport. Its default headers are user-agent, accept and accept-encoding, plus configured/request headers; the recipe adds Origin but no Fetch Metadata. This request is not a page-origin browser navigation or fetch and does not exercise browser CORS.
The /api/auth/ prefix returns through nextWithLocale before the generic API CORS and OPTIONS block. That branch adds common headers/locale cookie but does not declare foreign CORS access.
Only GET and POST are exported, with update-user alone intercepted; all other auth POSTs use the native handler.
Next auto-implements absent OPTIONS as204 with Allow; it does not add Access-Control-Allow-Origin. next.config.mjs adds COOP/CORP and security headers but no foreign CORS allowance.

source_predictions_not_runtime_results.prediction: Source provides no foreign-origin preflight grant; browser send/read behavior needs actual measurement. CORS failure must not be mistaken for general server-side write prevention.
Sign-in accepts this media type; browser cross-site/navigate Fetch Metadata should be rejected by formCsrfMiddleware. Must prove denied server-side effects and no session cookie/authority.
Fetch Metadata present should force strict trusted-origin matching even when Sec-Fetch-Site is same-site. Probe separate from cross-site.

source_predictions_not_runtime_results.transport: Cookie-free non-browser client with valid credentials and foreign Origin, no Fetch Metadata
source_predictions_not_runtime_results.prediction: Current source accepts credentials as observed. Whether this is intentionally supported is not established by the SDK implementation.

Historical analysis records partial CSRF coverage and a proposed helper; its older auth-stack description is not current runtime proof.
Tests configuration normalization, invalid values and absence of spoofed-host-derived trust; does not exercise cookie-free HTTP credential origin enforcement.
Current routing/private-transport tests do not qualify foreign-origin first-login browser behavior.
